root_cause.text: The rz-mtu3 counter driver's `rz_mtu3_count_enable_write()` lacked state validation for repeated sysfs enable/disable writes, so it re-executed enable/disable paths on an already enabled or disabled channel, corrupting runtime PM reference counting and operating on MTU3 hardware without proper ownership/state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mutex_lock(&priv->lock);` and an early check `if (priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] == enable) goto exit;`, while the CVE/commit states that every write to the sysfs enable file previously incremented/decremented the runtime PM counter, causing usage count underflow on repeated `0` writes, repeated increments on repeated `1` writes, register access with clocks off in `rz_mtu3_terminate_counter()`, and stopping PWM without the counter owning the channel.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The rz-mtu3 counter driver's `rz_mtu3_count_enable_write()` lacked state validation for repeated sysfs enable/disable writes, so it re-executed enable/disable paths on an already enabled or disabled channel, corrupting runtime PM reference counting and operating on MTU3 hardware without proper ownership/state.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `mutex_lock(&priv->lock);` and an early check `if (priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] == enable) goto exit;`, while the CVE/commit states that every write to the sysfs enable file previously incremented/decremented the runtime PM counter, causing usage count underflow on repeated `0` writes, repeated increments on repeated `1` writes, register access with clocks off in `rz_mtu3_terminate_counter()`, and stopping PWM without the counter owning the channel.

intent_record.intent_summary: Serialize counter enable-state changes and skip redundant enable or disable operations when the requested state is already active.
intent_record.what: The function now acquires priv->lock at the start, adds a check to compare priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] with the requested enable value and jumps to a new exit label if they already match, removes the duplicated mutex_lock/mutex_unlock calls from the enable and disable branches, and adds a single mutex_unlock at the common exit path before returning.
intent_record.how: This makes the enable/disable operation atomic across the state check and state transition, and avoids reinitializing or reterminating the counter when it is already in the requested state. At runtime, repeated requests for the current state now return immediately under the lock without calling pm_runtime_get_sync, rz_mtu3_initialize_counter, rz_mtu3_terminate_counter, or pm_runtime_put unnecessarily.

grouping_result.intent: Serialize counter enable-state changes and skip redundant enable or disable operations when the requested state is already active.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by validating/serializing enable-state transitions and ignoring redundant enable/disable requests, preventing repeated execution of paths that corrupt runtime PM reference counts and access hardware in the wrong state.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally increments the runtime PM usage count on every enable write, even when the channel is already enabled, directly causing PM reference count corruption described in the root cause.
This reinitializes the hardware on every enable request without validating whether the counter is already enabled, causing operations on MTU3 hardware without proper state/ownership checks.
This unconditionally terminates the counter on every disable write, even if already disabled, embodying the missing state validation and risking hardware manipulation in the wrong state.
This unconditionally decrements the runtime PM usage count on every disable write, even when the channel is already disabled, directly contributing to PM reference count imbalance.

vuln_statements.explanation: This enable-path call was executed unconditionally on sysfs writes without checking whether the channel was already enabled, directly causing runtime PM reference count corruption on repeated enable operations.
This disable-path call was executed unconditionally without validating that the channel was currently enabled, causing runtime PM reference count imbalance on repeated disable operations.

This reinitialized the MTU3 counter hardware on every enable request, even when the counter was already enabled, reflecting the missing state validation and operating on hardware without proper ownership/state checks.

This terminated the counter unconditionally on disable writes, including repeated disables when the channel was already off, embodying the missing enable-state validation and risking hardware operations in an invalid state.

Author: Biju Das <biju.das.jz@bp.renesas.com>

    counter: rz-mtu3-cnt: Reorder locking sequence for consistency
    
    All functions except rz_mtu3_count_enable_write(), call
    pm_runtime_{get,put} inside the lock. For consistency do the same here.
    
    Reported-by: Pavel Machek <pavel@denx.de>
    Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/r/ZH8Fmom8vZ4DwxqA@duo.ucw.cz

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full enable/disable logic relevant to the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present: on `if (enable)` the code unconditionally executes `pm_runtime_get_sync(ch->dev);`, `rz_mtu3_initialize_counter(counter, count->id);`, and then sets `priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] = true` only after initialization succeeds. There is no prior check such as `if (priv->count_is_enabled[count->id])` to reject or ignore repeated enable requests. Likewise, in the `else` path it unconditionally executes `rz_mtu3_terminate_counter(counter, count->id);`, sets `priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] = false;`, and calls `pm_runtime_put(ch->dev);` with no validation that the channel was actually enabled first. This matches the root cause: repeated sysfs enable/disable writes can re-run enable/disable paths and unbalance runtime PM references. The shown commit only reorders locking and PM calls (`pm_runtime_get_sync` moved inside the mutex on enable, and `pm_runtime_put` moved before `mutex_unlock` on disable) for consistency; it does not add state validation to prevent repeated enable/disable operations.

    phase counting modes on MTU1 and MTU2 channels

    2) 32-bit phase counting mode by cascading MTU1 and MTU2 channels.
    
    This patch adds 3 counter value channels.

The root cause is missing state validation for repeated enable/disable writes. In this function, the `enable` path unconditionally does `pm_runtime_get_sync(ch->dev);` and then calls `rz_mtu3_initialize_counter(counter, count->id);` before setting `priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] = true;`. There is no check like `if (priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] == enable) return 0;` or any equivalent guard to reject or ignore redundant writes. Likewise, the disable path unconditionally calls `rz_mtu3_terminate_counter(counter, count->id);`, sets `priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] = false;`, and then does `pm_runtime_put(ch->dev);`, again with no validation that the counter was actually enabled first. Because repeated writes to the same state will re-execute init/terminate and runtime PM get/put operations, this matches the stated root cause: corrupting runtime PM reference counting and operating on hardware without proper ownership/state. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
